related_questions.question: Does COVID start with a sore throat?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, a sore throat can be an early symptom of COVID-19, but it's not always the first or most prominent symptom. While a sore throat can be a common sign of various illnesses, including the common cold or strep throat, it's also a recognized symptom of COVID-19. In some cases, it may be one of the first symptoms experienced, but other symptoms like a runny nose, cough, body aches, fever, or fatigue may also be present.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, a sore throat can be an early symptom of COVID-19

text_blocks.snippet: If you experience a sore throat along with other COVID-19 symptoms, it's a good idea to get tested for COVID-19 and other potential causes like strep throat or influenza, according to GoHealth Urgent Care. Some specific Omicron subvariants, like NB.1.8.1 (Nimbus), can also cause particularly painful sore throats, according to WebMD.

Other common symptoms that may accompany a sore throat with COVID-19 include a runny nose, cough, body aches, fever, and fatigue, according to GoHealth Urgent Care. Some COVID-19 variants, like the Omicron subvariant NB.1.8.1 (Nimbus), are known for causing particularly painful sore throats, described as feeling like "razor blades" according to WebMD.
